topic: Land degradation and desertification — mixed tiers

questions.stem: The UN Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) is one of the three 'Rio Conventions'. The other two are the UNFCCC and:

options.option_text: Stockholm Convention
Convention on Biological Diversity
Basel Convention
Ramsar Convention

questions.explanation: The three 'Rio Conventions' — all born out of the 1992 Rio Earth Summit — are UNFCCC (climate), CBD (biodiversity) and UNCCD (desertification, signed 1994, in force 1996). India was a founder signatory of all three. Stockholm Convention (2001) targets persistent organic pollutants; Basel (1989) controls trans-boundary movement of hazardous waste; Ramsar (1971, pre-dates Rio) covers wetlands.

questions.stem: 'Chambal ravines' — classic example of land degradation by running water — are located mainly in:

options.option_text: Deccan plateau
MP / Rajasthan / UP border region
Gangetic plain
Eastern Ghats

questions.explanation: Chambal ravines / badlands stretch along the Chambal river in Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and parts of Uttar Pradesh — home to the National Chambal Sanctuary (protecting gharials, dolphins, turtles). The area was historically notorious for dacoit hideouts. Ravines form when concentrated rainwater cuts deep gullies into soft alluvium. National Bureau of Soil Survey estimates over 4 million ha of ravine-affected land in India.

questions.stem: The most important cause of soil erosion on agricultural land in India is:

options.option_text: Wind action
Running water (sheet and rill erosion)
Glacial retreat
Volcanic activity

questions.explanation: Running water is responsible for the vast majority of India's soil erosion — over 60 % of India's eroded land area. Monsoon rains on slopes without vegetation cover lift topsoil; sheet erosion (uniform loss across a slope) and rill erosion (small channels) are the most common forms. Wind erosion dominates only in the arid west (Thar, Kutch). Glacial and volcanic causes are negligible at the national scale.

questions.stem: 'Shifting cultivation' — locally called 'Jhum' in north-east India — is chiefly an issue because it causes:

options.option_text: Air pollution from cement factories
Deforestation and soil nutrient loss
Noise pollution
Water-logging

questions.explanation: Jhum (or swidden) — cut and burn small forest patches, cultivate for 2-3 years, move on. With adequate fallow (15-20+ years) the forest regenerates; but modern population pressure has shortened fallow to 3-5 years, leading to permanent forest loss, topsoil depletion, and sediment in streams. NE states and Odisha face this most. Government schemes (Mission Organic Value Chain, NE) promote settled agriculture as an alternative.

questions.stem: A scheme to reclaim sodic and saline soils in India, especially in Indo-Gangetic basin states, uses:

options.option_text: Lime (calcium oxide)
Gypsum (calcium sulphate)
Ammonium nitrate
Potash

questions.explanation: Gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O) is spread on sodic (high-sodium) soils — the Ca²⁺ displaces exchangeable Na⁺ on soil particles, which is then leached away by irrigation. Used on a large scale in UP, Haryana, Rajasthan. Lime (CaO / CaCO₃) is used on acidic soils (Kerala, NE hills) to raise pH. Ammonium nitrate and potash are fertilisers for nutrient deficiencies, not soil-chemistry reclamation.

options.option_text: Only afforestation is allowed by the Forest Conservation Act
Afforestation creates new forest where none existed recently; reforestation restores land that was forest
They mean the same thing
Reforestation uses only native species; afforestation uses only exotic species

questions.explanation: Afforestation — planting trees on land that has NOT been forested in recent historical memory (say 50+ years). Reforestation — restoring forest on land that was forested but has been cleared (logging, fire, land-change). Both are recognised in international climate accounting (UNFCCC). India's National Mission for a Green India (GIM), launched 2014, is one of eight missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change.

questions.stem: The 'land degradation neutrality' target set under the UNCCD aims to achieve no net loss of healthy land by:
questions.explanation: Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) is SDG Target 15.3 — 'By 2030, combat desertification, restore degraded land and soil, and strive to achieve a land-degradation-neutral world.' India committed at UNCCD COP-14 (Delhi, 2019) to restore 26 million hectares of degraded land by 2030 (up from the earlier 21 million hectare pledge). 2047 is India's 'Viksit Bharat' / Amrit Kaal target, 2050 the common net-zero deadline for climate.

questions.stem: In canal-irrigated plains of North India, secondary salinization of agricultural soils is primarily caused by which process?

options.option_text: Runoff carrying dissolved nitrogen from synthetic fertilizers
Evaporation of shallow saline groundwater depositing salts at the surface
Deforestation accelerating the rate of overland soil runoff
Overgrazing leading to permanent compaction of the topsoil layer

questions.explanation: Canal seepage raises the water table; as saline groundwater evaporates from near the surface, dissolved salts are left behind — a process called secondary salinization. Option A (fertilizer nitrogen runoff) causes eutrophication of water bodies, not salinization. Deforestation (C) accelerates erosion but not salt accumulation. Overgrazing (D) leads to desertification through compaction and vegetation loss, not salinization.

questions.stem: The Indira Gandhi Canal, while irrigating the Thar Desert margins, has caused an unintended land-degradation problem in adjacent areas. Which problem is this?

options.option_text: Severe gully erosion forming new ravine networks along the canal banks
Waterlogging and secondary salinization of surrounding agricultural land
Laterization of sandy desert soils within the canal command zone
Intensified wind erosion and reactivation of mobile sand dunes

questions.explanation: Seepage from the canal network raises the water table in adjoining fields. Shallow saline groundwater evaporates and deposits salts on the surface, causing waterlogging and salinization — a documented problem in Rajasthan's canal command area. Gully erosion (A) requires sloped terrain absent in the flat Thar plains. Laterization (C) needs high rainfall and temperature — conditions absent in Rajasthan. Mobile dune reactivation (D) is a pre-canal problem the project was designed to reduce.

questions.stem: India's National Action Programme to Combat Desertification (NAPCD) was prepared in 2001 as a national obligation under the UNCCD. Which ministry is the nodal agency responsible for it?

options.option_text: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (MoAFW)
Ministry of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj (MoRD)
Ministry of Jal Shakti (earlier Ministry of Water Resources)
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)

questions.explanation: Since UNCCD is a UN Environment Convention, India's NAPCD (2001) was prepared by the then Ministry of Environment and Forests — now MoEFCC. A common exam trap is attributing it to MoAFW (which administers soil health cards and fertilizer schemes) or MoRD (which runs the IWMP watershed programme). Jal Shakti (C) handles irrigation and drinking water. The Convention's environmental mandate makes MoEFCC the correct nodal ministry.

questions.stem: The Integrated Watershed Management Programme (IWMP), a major Centrally Sponsored Scheme for land restoration, was restructured in 2015 and merged into which programme?

options.option_text: Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana — Watershed Development component
Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana — soil conservation framework
National Watershed Development Project for Rainfed Areas (NWDPRA)
Mahatma Gandhi NREGS — natural resource management component

questions.explanation: In 2015, IWMP (administered by the Department of Land Resources under MoRD) was subsumed into Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) as its Watershed Development sub-programme, under the 'Har Khet Ko Pani, More Crop Per Drop' umbrella. NWDPRA (C) is an older predecessor scheme, not the successor. PMFBY (B) is a crop insurance scheme unrelated to watershed management. MGNREGS (D) does fund NRM works but is not the administrative successor to IWMP.

questions.stem: In the context of arid-zone geomorphology, 'deflation' refers to which specific land-degradation process?

options.option_text: Removal of surface soil by concentrated overland water flow
Lifting and long-distance transport of loose dry particles by wind
Downward migration of clay particles through the soil horizons
Loss of soil organic carbon from continuous monoculture farming

questions.explanation: Deflation is the wind-erosion process by which loose, dry, fine-grained particles (silt, clay, fine sand) are detached and carried away, leaving behind coarser 'lag gravel' or desert pavement — a key driver of desertification in the Thar and similar arid zones. Option A describes sheet or rill erosion (water process). Option C describes eluviation/clay illuviation within the soil profile. Option D describes soil exhaustion or nutrient depletion — not deflation.

questions.stem: The UNCCD's Science-Policy Interface (SPI) prescribes three globally agreed indicators for monitoring Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN). Which set correctly identifies all three?

options.option_text: Rainfall variability index, vegetation canopy density, soil salinity level
Forest cover percentage, groundwater recharge rate, crop productivity index
Soil organic carbon stock, land cover change, net primary productivity
Albedo ratio, evapotranspiration deficit, biodiversity intactness index

questions.explanation: The UNCCD SPI designated three complementary LDN indicators: (1) Land Cover Change — tracks conversion from natural/semi-natural to degraded states; (2) Land Productivity Dynamics (proxied by Net Primary Productivity/NPP) — reflects ecosystem functioning; and (3) Soil Organic Carbon (SOC) stock — proxy for soil health. Rainfall variability (A) is a pressure driver, not an LDN outcome indicator. Forest cover alone (B) misses non-forest degraded lands. Albedo/evapotranspiration (D) are research proxies but not the UNCCD's prescribed set.

questions.stem: The 'Great Green Wall' initiative aims to restore degraded land across approximately 8,000 km. Which geographic zone does it traverse, and which body provides primary institutional coordination?

options.option_text: Northern Arabian Peninsula coastline, coordinated by Arab League and UNEP
Central Asian Steppe corridor, coordinated by Shanghai Cooperation Organisation
Sahel belt of Africa (Senegal to Djibouti), led by the African Union
South American Gran Chaco region, coordinated by CELAC and the UNDP

questions.explanation: The Great Green Wall for the Sahara and Sahel Initiative (GGWSSI), launched in 2007, aims to grow a mosaic of restored land spanning the Sahel from Dakar (Senegal) on the Atlantic coast to Djibouti on the Red Sea. It is coordinated by the Pan-African Agency of the Great Green Wall under the African Union, with UNCCD, FAO, and World Bank providing support. Options A, B, and D are deliberate distractors pairing real regional bodies with the wrong geographic zones to test precision of recall.
